findings.evidence: grep: LimitSemigroup.lean:123,124,126 and :136,137,139 and LumerPhillips.lean:85,86 all contain `hA.mem_resolventSet h` / `simpa [one_div] using hA.norm_resolvent_le h`.
findings.fix: Reinstate `IsMDissipative.exp_yosidaApproximation_uniformCauchySeqOn_compact` and `IsMDissipative.tendsto_yosidaApproximation_apply_atTop` as one-line specializations (as the PR description itself says was done) and call them at the three sites.
findings.issue: The five-line block supplying the `M = K = 1` hypotheses (`(K := 1) (M := 1)`, `fun _ h => hA.mem_resolventSet h`, `by simpa [one_div] using hA.norm_resolvent_le h`, `norm_exp_smul_yosidaApproximation_le_one ...`) is repeated verbatim at lines 121-127 and 134-140, and its two-line prefix again at LumerPhillips.lean:84-86. The reusable fact — that an m-dissipative operator supplies the generalized hypotheses — is hidden in proof terms.

findings.evidence: Dense.lean:58-79 vs 112-137 are line-for-line the same argument modulo the name of the second operator.
findings.fix: Extract the shared core as a lemma, e.g. `‖T x - S x‖ ≤ ‖T y - S y‖ + K * ‖x - y‖ + K * ‖y - x‖` for `T S : X →L[𝕜] Y` with `‖T‖ ≤ K`, `‖S‖ ≤ K` (instantiate `S := g` in the first, `S := f j z` in the second), and reduce both proofs to choosing `y` and `linarith`.
findings.issue: `tendsto_apply_of_dense` (lines 36-79) and `uniformCauchySeqOn_apply_of_dense` (lines 87-137) are near-identical: same `K`, same `hscale`, same `exists_dist_lt`, same `hleft`/`hright` calc blocks, same `hdecomp`+`norm_add₃_le` finish, differing only in whether the second operator is `g` or `f j z`. Roughly 40 lines are duplicated, and both proofs sit at the 50-line threshold.

summary: Two factoring problems: the m-dissipative instantiation of the generalized Yosida lemmas is copy-pasted at three call sites instead of being a named specialization, and the two new density lemmas in Dense.lean repeat the same 3ε operator-comparison argument verbatim.
